messages:
nina (platform): quick sync — we need to pick a default internal transport for control-plane APIs and console surface. REST over JSON or gRPC/protobuf? thinking about routing policy ergonomics, quota propagation, telemetry fidelity, and rollout UX. thoughts?
omar (infra): my knee-jerk: gRPC for internal because of streaming + smaller payloads. but the gateway story and browser/console access complicates things.
sasha (console): +1 for ergonomics. console teams need easy fetches from browsers, but we can front gRPC with a gateway. main worry: telemetry and tracing need to survive the gateway translation.
kevin (sre): from ops POV: we want consistent headers for quotas/traces. If we go proto-first with a transcoding gateway, make sure trace-id, tenant, and route-claim headers are preserved and visible in metrics. otherwise console charts lie. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
priya (api): proto-first gives strong contracts and codegen for services, but quota binding semantics get tricky: do we attach quota tokens as metadata or in message fields? prefer header-based quota: x-redwood-tenant, x-route, x-quota-token. easier for Envoy policies.
mike (sdk): SDKs love codegen, but public SDKs and browser clients expect JSON-friendly endpoints. We could provide dual-surface: gRPC for backend-to-backend, JSON over gateway for browsers. important: keep identical semantics and error shapes.
omar (infra): note: gateway translation can change status semantics (gRPC status -> HTTP). we need a canonical mapping and a test harness. also streaming fallbacks are hairy — if client expects bidi, gateway can't help browsers.
nina (platform): on rollouts: can we do canary by transport? e.g., new service speaks gRPC; we route 10% of backend calls via gRPC path and 90% via HTTP transcoder. need telemetry signals to compare p95/p99, and quota burn rates per transport.
kevin (sre): yes — console should show per-transport breakdown in route dashboards. add a tag dimension: transport=grpc|http. Also want a sampled trace of a single request flow across gateway -> service.
sasha (console): UX ask: in rollouts view show delta-in-cost & delta-in-latency per route with button to compare request samplings. also surface how quotas would be charged differently if batching/streaming enabled.
priya (api): technical detail: header propagation through Envoy -> transcoder -> service: keep x-redwood-trace, x-tenant-id, x-route, x-client-version. envoys can copy but ensure transcoder won't drop unknown keys. add tests.
mike (sdk): small snippet for fallback check:
```
# curl fallback to transcoder
curl -H "x-redwood-tenant: acme" -H "x-redwood-trace: t-123" \ 
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood/svc/predict
```
priya (api): proto example for a route claim (very small):
```
service Predictor {
  rpc Predict(PredictRequest) returns (PredictReply);
}
message PredictRequest { string prompt = 1; string route = 2; }
```
Make sure route map is explicit so gateway can attach quota-route metadata.
omar (infra): ops concern: grpc connections keep long-lived connections and we need pool sizing + routing policies for multi-tenant. for Dedicated/private, gRPC wins; for hosted-console, gateway is necessary.
kevin (sre): also: quota enforcement point — do we enforce at gateway, service, or both? my vote: gateway enforces coarse quotas (per-tenant, per-route), service enforces token-level fine quotas. dup checks to avoid double-charge.
nina (platform): decision proposal: default internal transport = gRPC/protobuf for service-to-service. Expose JSON HTTP via a managed transcoding gateway for browser/partner clients. Requirements: header passthrough, transport tagging in telemetry, canonical error mapping, quota semantics doc, and rollout-by-transport tooling.
sasha (console): +1 but need API on console to opt into showing transport breakdown and a toggle to view only transcoded requests.
mike (sdk): will add generation for both surfaces. also we should auto-generate example cURL + JS fetch snippets for each route.
priya (api): I'll draft RFC with compatibility checklist: header whitelist, error mapping table, quota header names, streaming fallbacks, test harness.
marco (ci-bot): deploy check: lint rfc draft found 1 missing quota header in Predict example. please include `x-quota-key` in example.
priya (api): noted, will update. thanks marco.
kevin (sre): followup: let's add an alert when transcoder adds >5ms median overhead per route during canary. early warning prevents surprises.
nina (platform): perfect — Priya, can you get a draft RFC by EOD tomorrow? include a rollout checklist for platform, console, and infra.
priya (api): yes — will post RFC link here when ready.
omar (infra): I'll stub a small test harness that can replay traffic over both transports for metrics comparison.
sasha (console): thanks — will prototype console tiles for transport, delta-cost, and sampled traces.
mike (sdk): will plan dual-language examples.
nina (platform): thanks everyone. end state: proto-first internal, gateway for external, full telemetry & quota contract. brief follow-ups in RFC. :rocket:
